This tutorial answers four questions on one small simulation: which coordinates
to read factors in, what the posterior uncertainty means, how a sample-group
contrast translates into feature units, and how to fit and filter nonnegative
gene programs. The simulated sample is the independent unit; there is no real
biology. [Get started](first-fit.html) defines view, activity, effects and
offset.

## Coordinates

A fit has one reconstruction but many equivalent coordinate systems. `"raw"`
keeps flashier's own scaling. `"ldf"` (the default) gives unit-norm factors with
the scale on one side. `"rms"` gives every activity column unit root-mean-square
so activities are comparable across factors. Pick one and keep its activity and
effects together.

```{r setup}
library(flashier.utils)
set.seed(17)
A <- matrix(rnorm(80), 40, 2)
B <- matrix(rnorm(24), 12, 2)
X <- tcrossprod(A, B) + matrix(rnorm(480, sd = .2), 40, 12)
dimnames(X) <- list(paste0("s", 1:40), paste0("g", 1:12))
fit <- flashier::flash(X, greedy_Kmax = 2, nullcheck = FALSE,
  ebnm_fn = ebnm::ebnm_normal, backfit = TRUE, verbose = 0)
raw <- standardize_factors(fit, sample_side = "rows", scaling = "raw",
                           feature_scale = "simulated_intensity")
view <- standardize_factors(fit, sample_side = "rows", scaling = "rms",
                            feature_scale = "simulated_intensity")
stopifnot(max(abs(tcrossprod(raw$activity, raw$effects) -
                  tcrossprod(view$activity, view$effects))) < 1e-8)
```

```{r coordinates-figure, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, fig.alt="Boxplots of activity per factor under raw and RMS scaling. Raw spreads differ between F1 and F2; RMS makes them equal.", fig.cap="Activity of all 40 simulated samples per factor in raw and RMS coordinates (points) with a box summary. Same fit, same reconstruction, different units; RMS forces unit root-mean-square per factor."}
library(ggplot2)
activity_long <- rbind(cbind(scaling = "raw", as.data.frame(as.table(raw$activity))),
                       cbind(scaling = "rms", as.data.frame(as.table(view$activity))))
names(activity_long)[2:4] <- c("sample", "factor", "activity")
ggplot(activity_long, aes(factor, activity)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~scaling) + theme_minimal()
```

RMS scaling changes factor units while preserving their product. LDF scaling
also preserves the product, with its diagonal absorbed on exactly one side.
Always use the matching activity/effect pair and retain `view$offset` when
reconstructing an affine model: `sweep(tcrossprod(A, B), 2, offset, "+")`.
Do not mix coefficients or posterior draws from different bases.

## Conditional uncertainty

Posterior standard deviations come from the native fit, expressed in the
coordinates of the view you pass.

```{r uncertainty, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, fig.alt="Point ranges of each feature effect plus or minus one posterior standard deviation, one panel per factor. Ranges are narrow relative to the effects.", fig.cap="Feature effects for the 12 simulated genes with ± 1 posterior SD, conditional on the estimated priors and fitted rank (mean-field, typically too narrow). Not a regression standard error."}
effect_sd <- factor_uncertainty(fit, side = "effects", sample_side = "rows",
                                representation = view)
ggplot(effect_sd, aes(feature, estimate)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = estimate - posterior.sd, ymax = estimate + posterior.sd)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + facet_wrap(~factor) + theme_minimal()
head(factor_uncertainty(fit, side = "activity", sample_side = "rows",
                        representation = view))
```

Keep the native fit for posterior moments and sampling; a representation alone
contains coordinates, not a posterior sampler. Native uncertainty is conditional
on estimated priors. It is neither a downstream regression standard error nor
uncertainty about the biological identity of a factor.

## Group contrast in feature units

First summarize and contrast factor activity by a metadata column.

```{r contrast, fig.width=7, fig.height=3, fig.alt="Boxplots of activity by group A and B for each factor.", fig.cap="Activity by sample group. The descriptive contrast below summarizes these distributions."}
metadata <- data.frame(sample = rownames(X), donor = rownames(X),
                       group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20))
plot_factor_activity(view, metadata = metadata, group = "group", style = "distribution")
head(summarize_factor_activity(view, metadata, by = "group", unit_col = "donor"))
contrast <- compare_factor_groups(view, metadata, group = "group",
                                  contrast = c("A", "B"), unit_col = "donor")
names(contrast)
```

`c("A", "B")` means A minus B. Group summaries are descriptive and default to
observation weighting; cells are not automatically balanced by donor.
Threshold summaries use resolved activity coordinates. Display normalization
must not silently redefine an inferential threshold.

Then test each factor against the design and push the fitted coefficient back
through the effects to get a per-feature contrast.

```{r association}
association <- test_factors(view, metadata, formula = ~group, engine = "lm",
                            unit_col = "donor", independence = "independent")
reconstructed <- backproject_contrast(view, association$table,
  input = "coefficients", factor_basis = view$manifest, term = "groupB")
head(reconstructed$effects)
```

```{r backprojection-figure, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, fig.alt="Bar chart of the backprojected B minus A contrast per feature.", fig.cap="Backprojected group contrast per simulated gene in simulated intensity units (B minus A; 20 independent samples per group). Point estimates only; no uncertainty is attached."}
ggplot(reconstructed$effects, aes(feature, estimate)) + geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + theme_minimal() + labs(y = "B − A")
```

Here `groupB` means B minus A, opposite to the descriptive contrast above.
Backprojection multiplies feature effects by factor coefficients; offsets cancel
in a same-model contrast. Point coefficients alone supply no uncertainty.
Use a full coefficient covariance or compatible draws when justified; factor
posterior SDs cannot substitute for either. Repeated observations require an
appropriate repeated-unit model, not an independent-cell test.

For observed feature contrasts, `validate_backprojection()` requires matching
contrast direction, covariates, weighting and feature units. It reports descriptive
agreement, not independent biological validation. Named scientific arguments are
preferred; see function references for complete controls.

## Choose `ebnm_fn`, `S` and `var_type`

Choose `ebnm_fn` from the support your measurements require. Nonnegative
activities can pair with signed effects in Gaussian EBMF. A Poisson topic model
instead models nonnegative counts with mixed memberships. `S` specifies supplied
noise; `var_type` decides which residual variances the Gaussian model estimates.
`S = .5, var_type = NULL` fixes supplied noise. `S = .5, var_type = 0`
also estimates residual variance. `max_factors` is the EBMF greedy upper bound;
GBCD uses its distinct `kmax` argument. Initialization and backfit affect the
numerical optimum, so compare seeds without treating agreement as calibration.

Jiadong Mao's [EBNMF workshop](https://jiadongm.github.io/EBNMF-workshop/EBNMF.html)
explains EBNM shrinkage, prior families, EBMF, topic models and GBCD.
Use those explanations alongside the original package manuals. No workshop
code or prose is copied here; its repository has no identified license.

## Filter cells by total GP membership

[ImmGenT-GP section 5](https://aguerozz.github.io/immgenT-GP-analysis/Methods_FlashierFit.html#5_Cell_filtering_by_total_GP_membership)
removes cells with excessive total maximum-scaled membership. Each pass
recomputes GP maxima after removal. The pipeline uses 12 passes and cutoff 10.
Ziang Zhang / AgueroZZ provided the workflow; per-script authorship is unresolved.
This package independently implements that rule without copying upstream code.

```{r membership-filter}
nonnegative_fit <- fit_ebmf(X, "rows", max_factors = 2,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_normal),
  nullcheck = FALSE, backfit = TRUE, seed = 18, verbose = 0)
filtered <- filter_cells_by_total_membership(nonnegative_fit, max_val = 10, numiter = 12)
filtered$removed_samples
```

```{r membership-figure, fig.width=6, fig.height=2.5, fig.alt="Step chart of samples remaining after each of the twelve filtering passes.", fig.cap="Samples remaining after each discrete pass (steps, not a continuous trend). The count stops changing once no sample exceeds the cutoff."}
ggplot(filtered$history, aes(iteration, remaining)) + geom_step() + geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = filtered$history$iteration) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) + theme_minimal() + labs(y = "samples remaining")
```

Activities must be nonnegative. Signed feature effects remain valid. The result
contains matched sample activities and feature effects with unchanged retained
reconstruction. The original fit stays unchanged. Selected-cell PVE and posterior
uncertainty require separate analysis. This threshold selects broad GP membership;
it does not establish poor cell quality.

## Fit GBCD programs

GBCD fits cell covariance before estimating gene signatures with fixed memberships.
Yusha Liu, Peter Carbonetto, Jason Willwerscheid and Matthew Stephens wrote
[gbcd](https://github.com/stephenslab/gbcd). This adapter calls their engine.
Install the audited optional version outside package builds:

```{r gbcd-install, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("stephenslab/gbcd@670e3afb50236303ddf99db33a3394abd4a711bd")
```

Supply normalized natural-log expression. Declare its preprocessing explicitly.
The wrapper performs no normalization. `kmax` controls upstream initialization;
it does not cap final rank. The memory preflight predicts upstream allocation
branches, but cannot guarantee a peak-memory bound.

```{r gbcd-workflow, eval=FALSE}
programs <- fit_gbcd_programs(X, "rows", kmax = 5,
  feature_scale = "natural_log",
  preprocessing = list(scope = "within_dataset",
    description = "log1p library-size normalized counts", log_base = "e"))
view <- programs$representation
factor_features(view, "GEP1", select = "distinctive")
plot_factor_features(view, "GEP1")
programs$signatures
programs$diagnostics
provenance(result = programs)
```

Factors are named `GEP1`, `GEP2`, ... (gene expression programs). `effect` and
`log2_fc` describe EB-SNMF point estimates. `z_score` and `lfsr` (local false
sign rate) come from separate gene-wise linear regression followed by ashr.
These statistics condition on estimated memberships. They do not measure
uncertainty in learning those memberships. Unavailable statistics remain `NA`.
Native FLASH PVE and posterior sampling remain unavailable for this
representation.

The upstream `Baseline` label remains a varying factor. It is never converted
to a constant offset. Output sorting loses prior lineage, so every returned
activity support stays unknown. Default projection priors cannot be inferred.

## Grade-of-membership differential expression

Workshop section 5.5 uses `fastTopics::de_analysis()` for grade-of-membership
(GoM) DE. That method requires count data and nonnegative memberships whose
rows sum to one. `test_gom_de()` calls it after checking both inputs, with a
required seed. It estimates topic expression with fixed memberships and reports
least-extreme log2 fold changes with conditional uncertainty. See the
[original fastTopics manual](https://stephenslab.github.io/fastTopics/reference/de_analysis.html)
and package authors Peter Carbonetto, Kevin Luo, Kushal Dey and Matthew Stephens.
Abhishek Sarkar and other contributors also receive credit in the package.
`factor_features(select = "distinctive")` instead ranks descriptive coefficient
margins in the supplied factor basis. Those margins have no GoM DE lfsr.
GBCD's separate LM/ash statistics also differ from count-based GoM DE.
